title: SR-1.23 verify() catches a removed tail of the active segment and a removed last record of a path
request: Closes G88: removing the last records of the unsealed segment leaves a valid prefix, so verify() reports no gap in 10 of 10 cases although snapshot.json records a higher sequence; a removed or rehashed last record of a path is never caught (src/engine/oplog.mjs:218-234), against the file's own comments that every seal and per-path chain is checked. Found by the memev twin on 30 October 2026 at main be457db (a sealed run in the twin's evidence). Repository: memev. Depends on contracts: SR-1.01, QL-1.02. Sensitive path (the oplog): the QL-1.03 checklist applies before merge.

tasks.title: Tail and last-record checks
requirements: verify() fails when the snapshot's recorded sequence is higher than the last record on disk, naming both numbers
verify() fails when a path's head in the snapshot does not match the last record of that path on disk
the comments at the top of oplog.mjs describe exactly what verify() checks

the head check compares the hash and type of each path's last record on disk with the snapshot's head for that path, deleted heads included, so a rewritten record with the same seq, ts and prev, or a delete swapped for a put, fails

the tail check compares the snapshot's seq with the highest seq of any complete record on disk across every segment, never with a file size: blank lines are skipped, and an empty or missing active segment counts as holding no record

open() never lowers a segment's recorded last seq in manifest.json; verify() reports a segment whose highest seq on disk is below its recorded last, naming both numbers, so deleting snapshot.json does not hide a cut tail; a missing snapshot alone stays acceptable
verify() is read-only: it never changes this.seq, this.heads, a segment, archive/, manifest.json or snapshot.json, and two calls in a row return the same errors
verify() judges each path against the records it reads in one pass, so records another process appends after this instance opened are never reported as a mismatch
verify() streams the segments and holds only the per-path heads in memory, whatever the size of the log
the tail and head errors come before the per-record errors in verify().errors, so the 20-error cut never drops them

the header comment of oplog.mjs names the snapshot and manifest comparisons and states their limits: records written after the last snapshot are not covered, and snapshot.json carries no key, so a writer of the log folder can rewrite it consistently; records without a path get no chain and no head check

open() never lets this.seq fall below the highest last seq any segment records in manifest.json, and append() never lowers a segment's recorded last, so the next append after a cut tail leaves a seq gap that verify() reports

the head check reads the heads from snapshot.json on disk and compares each with the last record of that path at or below the snapshot's seq, never with this instance's in-memory heads, so a rewritten snapshot-covered record is caught even when the path has later records

verify() reads manifest.json and snapshot.json fresh from disk as one consistent pair (the manifest is read again after the snapshot, and the pair is read again if it changed) into local variables, judges the segments that fresh manifest lists, and never assigns this.manifest, this.active, this.sinceSnapshot, this.recovered or this.clock

verify() never throws for a damaged log: a missing segment file, an archived segment missing from archive/, a line that parses to anything but a record object, and an active segment deleted while the log is open are each reported as an error naming the segment or the seqs

open() skips and reports a line after the snapshot offset that parses to anything but a record object (null, a number, an array), as it does for an unreadable line, so such a line never stops the vault opening
a test that checks that an error names a number matches it as a whole word
